title: Hilltop Access Road, Kennewick, Washington
description: An example road plan: a single-lane gravel access road for maintenance trucks, from the end of the road stub off W 47th Ave at the foot of a hill at the south edge of Kennewick, Washington, to a level site on the hilltop. The plan illustrates Roadie on USGS lidar terrain - it isn't a proposed project.

**The site.** The road end is at 933 feet and the hilltop is at 1,137 feet - a 204 foot climb in 1,090 feet, straight up the hill's north face, which is a 19% grade. A road within the 12% maximum grade has to be nearly twice that long, so both options climb east across the north face (its side slopes are 25% to 50%) and come around the hill's gentle east shoulder to the top.
**Design criteria.** A rural access road: 14 feet wide, gravel, 12% maximum grade (the options are designed at 11%), 50 foot minimum curve radius, with turnouts.
**Features added to the site.** The USGS maps show no streams or roads on the hill, so these are from the lidar terrain and the topographic map:
- Two draws, as streams - the West draw (it drains 13 acres of the hill) and the East draw (4 acres). The options cross the East draw, with a culvert.
- The house lots west of the road end, as an exclusion area - an assumption, from the buildings on the topographic map.

- The Hilltop track, as an existing road - an unmapped dirt track up the east shoulder to the hilltop. Its worn trough shows in the lidar terrain. Its condition, and whether the road may use it, must be verified in the field.

**Options not kept.** A road west across the West draw (cost score 293.1, with a 17 foot cut) and two attempts at switchbacks up the north face (cost scores 283.1 and 382.0 - both doubled back across the hill) cost about twice the options kept, and were no better in any other way.
**Limitations.** The turnaround at the hilltop isn't modeled. Property lines and utilities aren't known. The Hilltop track continues east beyond the site.

sources.name: USGS 3D Elevation Program 1 meter elevation model WA_ColumbiaValley_2018_D19

options.name: Hilltop Track
description: The least-cost option. A new road climbs east from the road end across the hill's north face, crosses the East draw with a 3 foot culvert at station 6+12, and comes around the east shoulder to the Hilltop track - then it follows the track for 539 feet (stations 15+88 to 21+27) to the hilltop, where the last 210 feet are new road.
- 2,337 feet long at an 11% maximum grade, with four turnouts
- Its cuts are 4 feet at most, and its fills 2 feet. It excavates 1,602 cubic yards and wastes 1,010.
- The curve onto the track was eased by hand, to a 79 foot radius - the route search's was 45 feet, under the 50 foot minimum.
The track is costed as an existing road upgrade (reshaping and a gravel lift), with no earthwork - its as-built grade is about 10%. If the track can't be used, the New Road option is the fallback.

options.name: New Road
description: An all-new road, for comparison - the same climb across the north face and around the east shoulder, then its own line below the Hilltop track to the hilltop from the southeast.
- 2,435 feet long at an 11% maximum grade, with six turnouts and a 3 foot culvert at the East draw (station 6+23)
- Its cuts and fills are under 5 feet. It excavates 2,260 cubic yards and wastes 1,597.
- It costs a quarter more than the Hilltop Track option - its last 900 feet are new road where that option upgrades the track.
